name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 6, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Leckness at 5:02 p.m., on October 6, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 1, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

  Absent:  Council Member Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

Council Member Schlicht expressed concern about the legality of a closed session for a private
property discussion.

City Attorney Curley stated that the Council gave staff prior direction, an appraisal has been
pursued and he noted that the Council does not talk about price and terms in public.

 CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel--Anticipated Litigation Based on existing facts and
  circumstances, the Successor Agency, City Council, and Financing Authority will
  confer with legal counsel and provide direction regarding (i) whether or not to

City Council Minutes  1  October 6, 2014
   initiate litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(c) - one potential case, and (ii)
  significant exposure to litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(d) - one potential case.

 CS2. Conference With Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property: That Portion of Oso Creek Trail System Owned by American
  Golf (The Open Space Located Between Casta Del Sol Road and Jeronimo Road -
  The Tennis Pavilion to the West and the Casta Del Sol Residential Community to
  the East.) City Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg and Assistant City
  Manager Keith Rattay. Owner’s Negotiators: American Golf President. Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:08 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was
absent.)

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that for item CS1, the Council gave direction to staff but will not
be commencing action. For item CS2, the Council considered some information but took no
action. The issue will be addressed again at some future date.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim October 5 through October 11, 2014 To Be Fire Prevention Week

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Battalion Chief Steve Edwards.

P2.  Recognize Paramedic Michael Curtis for Risking his Life to Save a Suicidal Man

  Mayor Kelley presented a certificate of commendation to Michael Curtis.

P3.  Wounded Warriors Presentation

  The City Council and audience received a presentation from Victor Gonzalez.

RECESS

At the hour of 6:36 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:43
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

City Council Minutes  2  October 6, 2014
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tammy Descoteaux, M.V.: invited residents and the Council Members to the Walk Against Drugs
on Saturday, October 18, 2014, at Mission Viejo High School, beginning at 8:00 a.m.

Carol Weidler, M.V.: expressed outrage at a flier regarding E-Cigarettes That was left on her car
at a community event. She stated that the flier contains inaccuracies and the authors didn't even
have the courage to sign it.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: read a sample list of questions that he wrote for city council candidate
debates and he recommended that the Rotary Club consider using some of the questions in its
upcoming candidate forum.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 4, 6, 7, 11, 12 and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Fourth Quarter of
  FY 2013-14

  Received and filed.

5.  Check Register Dated September 12, 2014 in the Amount of $385,297.54

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Semi-annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  - For the Year Ended June 30, 2014

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  October 6, 2014
 9.  Orange County Transportation Authority 2014-2015 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  Adopted Resolution 14-45 Approving the Submittal of the Alicia Parkway Corridor and
  Olympiad Road/Felipe Road Corridor Improvement Projects to the Orange County
  Transportation Authority for Funding Under the Competitive Measure M2 Regional
  Transportation Signal Synchronization Program (Project P).

10.  Request for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption"
  regulation at City Facilities for the Lululemon Grand Opening Tennis Social and the
  2014 Uniqlo Wheelchair Doubles Masters Tennis Tournament.

  Approved a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" regulation
  at City Facilities for the Lululemon Grand Opening Tennis Social October 27th and the
  UNIQLO Wheelchair Doubles Masters November 5-9, 2014 at the Marguerite Tennis
  Pavilion.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she would abstain from the vote on this item
  because she was absent from the September 15 City Council Meeting.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 15, 2014, as
  presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Ury
  ABSTAIN: Schlicht

4.  Check Register Dated September 5, 2014 in the Amount of $840,077.42

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff to get back to her with details on a $1,000 bill from
  Lozano Smith for the library.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  October 6, 2014
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

6.  Check Register dated September 19, 2014 in the amount of $1,159,863.53

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about bills for La Paws Park for emergency repairs and
  re-turf. She asked what emergency the city had at that location.

  City Manager Wilberg indicated that he would get back to the Council Members with a
  detailed response.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

7.  Year-End Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Twelve Months Ended
  June 30, 2014

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her concern that the city just wiped out $100,000 in debt
  without any idea how a $400,000 gift to the Mission Viejo Foundation was spent. She also
  registered her issue with discretionary reserves and asked for clarification of the last
  paragraph in the staff report.

  Director Dyas provided an explanation of the Council's action in January 2014 relative to the
  retiree insurance program and the 800 MHz system.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

11. Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Agreement

  Council Member Schlicht asked what orthophotography is and what were the modifications
  to the agreement since this was addressed the last time.

City Council Minutes  5  October 6, 2014
   City Attorney Curley responded that the business terms haven't changed, but the city contract
  has now been included with the vendor contract.

  Public Works Director Chagnon announced that orthophotography is aerial mapping of the
  City which is updated every few years.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  approve agreement with Digital Map Products, Inc. for a one-year initial term and two one
  year renewal options for a total term not to exceed three years in the amount of $42,419 per
  year for the purchase of services and data.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

12. Federal-Aid Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant: Citywide
  Emergency Vehicle Pre-emption (EVP) System Installation Project (CIP 215)

  Mayor Kelley commended staff for the proactive attempt to fight for dollars that can be used
  in Mission Viejo for EVP devices.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon provided a staff report.

  Mayor Kelley provided a history of the EVP devices and award of the grant.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1) approve the
  bid specifications for the subject project; and (2) authorize staff to advertise for construction
  bids for the installation of emergency vehicle pre-emption (EVP) system devices on existing
  traffic signal infrastructure.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

13. Orange County Transportation Authority Arterial Pavement Management Program
  Application: Marguerite Parkway and Trabuco Road

  Council Member Schlicht asked why the City stopped paving where it did instead of
  continuing north to El Toro Road and out to the city boundaries.

  Director Chagnon responded Trabuco Road was just recently paved to the north city
  boundary. He noted that the pavement condition on Marguerite Parkway did not qualify for

City Council Minutes  6  October 6, 2014
   the grant application requirements but it could be added to the scope of the project and the
  city could fund that portion.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 14-46 Authorizing Application for Funds for the Arterial Pavement
  Management Program Funded with Regional Surface Transportation Program Funding
  Under the Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Federal Transportation Act for the
  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation Project; and (2) authorize
  the City Manager to enter into an Agreement with the Orange County Transportation
  Authority and the California Department of Transportation to receive said funds.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: reported that concerns of the senior citizen community about
  ambulance rebates have been heard by county and state officials.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury was absent therefore no report was given.

16. Orange County Vector Control District

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented the report.

17. SCAG Transportation Committee (TC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that residents who take the time to write a letter are entitled to
a response. He noted that he is still awaiting a response to his June 2, 2014, letter regarding the
City's financial obligation regarding the OCFA's unfunded liability.

City Council Minutes  7  October 6, 2014
 18.  Close Out of FY 2013/14 and FY 2014/15 Budget Adjustments

City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report and Director of Administrative Services
Cheryl Dyas answered the City Council Member's questions.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
adopt Resolution 14-47 Amending the FY 2013/14 City Budget for Year-End Close Out
Adjustments in Certain Accounts and Funds; and (2) adopt Resolution 14-48 Amending the
FY 2014/15 City Budget.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

RECESS

At the hour of 8:21 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:29
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she will have a very extensive TCA report at the next
City Council Meeting. She noted that TCA Agendas and Minutes will be posted on their website
as recommended by the Grand Jury and the agency will also post meeting videos online in the near
future. Council Member Reardon discussed her attendance at the City’s Emergency Management
Academy as well as an ACC-OC meeting on emergency preparedness. She stated that there is
nothing really new about being prepared and there is plenty of information available for residents
about earthquake preparedness. Also, OCFA has a “Ready Set Go” program which teaches people
to protect their homes from wildfires and the City offers a Community Emergency Preparedness
Academy (CEPA) each year. The dates for the 2015 CEPA will be announced in January. Council
Member Reardon outlined her attendance at the KSBR show last weekend where Library Director
Genesis Hansen spoke eloquently and in detail on the use of technology at the library and the
impact that they are having on kids in the community. Council Member Reardon encouraged
residents to get on the library website if they would like to find out what opportunities are available
at the library. Lastly, Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at the Orange County
Automobile Dealers Association meeting where Ben Stein spoke. She said that it‘s always a

City Council Minutes  8  October 6, 2014
 pleasure to go to those events and she learned that Orange County auto dealers are coming back
with vigor.

Council Member Schlicht

20.  Double Fault on 2013 ITF Contracts: The lack of accountability led to the by-passing
  of the city council on expenditures for this pet project cannot be repeated with the
  upcoming 2014 International Tennis Federation (ITF) Wheelchair Doubles Masters

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: made recommendation regarding the budget for the event, staff
  accountability and the discontinuation of sponsorships.

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to put
  in place mechanisms to ensure transparency in the performance of the Contract to Host the
  2014 International Tennis Federation (ITF) Wheelchair Doubles Masters; to properly plan
  and execute the contract; to promote economical expenditures of public monies to prevent
  unauthorized growth of the budget; to ensure that public funds are spent for a public
  purpose; to timely report to the council and the public the results of the tennis tournament.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

21.  Preventing Abuse of Public Resources for Re-Election Advantage

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Carol Weidler, M.V.: stated that it is because of the Mission Viejo City Council that she
  became aware of the potential dangers and latest drug problems with teens. She stated that
  a movie alerting parents and grandparents to drug dangers in the community is not a political
  statement and she thanked the City Council for bringing the message to the residents.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, to delay all publicity and pull down all links to
  MVTV series "An Invisible Line: Teen Drug Abuse in our Community" hosted by City
  Councilmember and Candidate Rhonda Reardon. The motion died for lack of a second.

Council Member Schlicht asked the City Clerk about an email that was sent to a City Council
candidate on the subject of traffic signals which the City Clerk forwarded to the Council Members
this afternoon. She asked if the email was shared with all of the City Council candidates. City
Clerk Karen Hamman responded that the referenced email was not sent to the other candidates
however they were told, when they pulled nomination paperwork, that all candidate requests for
information from staff are always available at their asking. Council Member Schlicht noted that in

City Council Minutes  9  October 6, 2014
 the past, all inquiries were sent to all Council candidates. City Clerk Hamman noted that staff used
to maintain a notebook with copies of all requests but now they are retained electronically and they
are publicly available to the candidates and anyone who asks.

Council Member Schlicht asked the City Clerk if the candidate’s 460 campaign finance forms can
be placed in the candidate log on the City’s website. City Clerk Hamman responded that the forms
will be posted on the candidate log and they are also available online in the Sire document
management system.

Relating to an earlier discussion, City Attorney Curley noted that Council Member Schlicht asked
if staff will attach the appeal pleadings for the OCFA equity matter. Mr. Curley has learned that
no briefs have been filed to date but they should be filed in a few weeks. Depending on the timing,
there may or may not be pleadings to attach to the report when the OCFA Resolutions come back
at the next Council Meeting.

Council Member Schlicht announced that at the next Council Meeting she will adjust the tyranny
of the Council majority that passed agenda items under her name without discussion at the last
meeting when she was absent. She stated that that action shows contempt towards open and
transparent government and she will be bringing those agenda items back at the next meeting.
Council Member Schlicht stated that she is happy that her colleagues supported her agenda item
regarding the ITF wheelchair masters oversight and budget on tonight’s agenda. Regarding E-
cigarettes, she stated that Council Member Reardon attempted to punish minors for possession E-
cigarettes with a recent agenda item and she stated that the punishment would have exceeded the
rate of the crime. Council Member Schlicht noted that she cannot find a law anywhere in the nation
that makes it illegal for anyone in the country, regardless of age, to smoke E-cigarettes however the
State of California makes it an infraction for a person to furnish an E-cig to a minor, not a
misdemeanor as Council Member Reardon’s agenda item proposed.

City Attorney Curley stopped Council Member Schlicht and stated that she is essentially
communicating her position on the matter outside of a hearing and he noted that the topic could be
coming back to the City Council. Mr. Curley stated that Council Member Schlicht is predicting her
vote with her current line of statements and he recommended that it is better to wait and see if the
matter comes back before she says any more.

Council Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at recent events including the Vietnam Veteran
luncheon where she sat with sailors and marines. She noted that it was a wonderful event honoring
wonderful people who allow the Council to sit at the dais and protect our nation’s liberties. Council
Member Schlicht thanked Bill Cook and his “A Team” for supporting a Veterans Cemetery at the
Irvine Great Park which the Governor approved on Saturday, September 27. She also thanked her
colleagues for supporting her resolution to support Prop 13 at a prior meeting. Council Member
Schlicht announced that the county is offering a public hearing on the Common Core curriculum
where proponents and opponents will provide information and there will be a question and answer
period and the public will have an opportunity to speak. The hearings will be held in Costa Mesa
on October 20 and November 17, 2014, from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. In closing, Council Member
Schlicht dedicated her quote to two people: 9/11 Hero Todd Beamer and Bob Galin, her favorite

City Council Minutes  10  October 6, 2014
 boss. “There are some who bring a light so great to the world that even after they are gone, the light
remains.”

Council Member Ury

22.  Permit fee Waiver Program for Water Conservation Improvements

  Council Member Ury was absent therefore this item was continued to the next City Council
  Meeting.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

23.  MVTV Programming

  Council Member Leckness presented his report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to direct staff to
  return to the Council in 30-60 days with creative ideas and a budget for future MVTV
  programming.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ury

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to direct staff to
  meet with the new KSBR station director or the appropriate college representative and return
  to the City Council with a report within 30-60 days.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley asked staff to provide an update or review on the procedures for taking care of
turning off athletic field lights at night. Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix
outlined the process noting that all lights are programmed to come on automatically for all
scheduled games. The lights are programmed around the leagues’ requests and typically turn on
15 minutes before dusk. The lights turn off when the game permit ends. Mr. Nix said that the
athletic groups have a password so they can call and have the lights turned off when their games
are over. Staff constantly reminds the youth sports groups to review the process with coaches and
make sure that the lights are turned off. Council Member Schlicht asked if the lights can be turned

City Council Minutes  11  October 6, 2014
 off from a computer. Mr. Nix responded that they can. Mayor Kelley asked if members of the
public can call for lights to be turned off. Mr. Nix recommended that residents email the recreation
department if they see lights on at an empty field as those emails are monitored by staff even after
business hours. Mr. Wilberg recommended that if residents see lights left on, they should notify
the City so that staff can contact the league responsible for the field at that time.

Mayor Kelley announced that the Mission Viejo Today program, highlight the City’s wonderful
library, is now on the city website and Mission Viejo Television and she encouraged residents to
look for that program. Mayor Kelley stated that the Vietnam Veterans recognition program was a
huge success and she commended Director Nix and his staff for their efforts. She also outlined
her attendance at the Saddleback College State of the College address and she noted that there was
a wealth of good information and she is proud that Mission Viejo is the home of a first class
community college. Mayor Kelley reminded residents that the 26th Annual Walk Against Drugs
will be held on October 18, 2014, beginning at 8:00 a.m. She recommended that attendees get
there early for parking or take the bus from Newhart Middle School. The drug walk will end with
a Disaster Preparedness Expo at Oso Viejo Park behind the Murray Center. Finally, Mayor Kelley
discussed her attendance at the Palmia community’s 25th anniversary and she thanked Bob and
Sandy Haig and the committee who organized the event.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:40 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of her brother-in-law, Jim Kelley, and the five
teens who were tragically killed in a car accident on October 11: Alex Sotelo, Matthew Melo,
Brandon Moreno, Jenny Campos, and Jennifer Bahena. The next City Council Meeting will be
held on Monday, October 20, 2014, beginning at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 20, 2014

City Council Minutes  12  October 6, 2014
